characters.name: Lady Evelyn Vance
characters.special: YOU ARE ON THE SHADOW TEAM! You are allied with Clara Sterling (#2) and win ONLY if the Killer escapes indictment in the Final Verdict. Fellow accomplice: Harriet Vance-Cole (#8). Wake up with the Shadow Team during Blackout Phases.
characters.persona: Sharp-tongued, glamorous heiress. At 8:30 PM, you had a furious public argument with Arthur about being disinherited and shouted, 'You'll regret this before nine!'
characters.secret: You are secretly tied to Clara Sterling's (#2) 2008 cover-up and helped keep the upstairs gallery clear from 8:10–8:20 PM while Clara Sterling rigged the Automaton. Protect Clara Sterling in Town Hall votes!
characters.clue: STRATEGY: Deflect suspicion onto Victor Vance (#5) and defend Clara Sterling's (#2) 8:55 PM Grand Hall alibi!
characters.detention: Searched from Lady Evelyn Vance's Belongings: A burner phone with an unsent draft: 'C.S. — Upstairs corridor clear 8:10 to 8:20 PM. Stop Archive Box #4 at any cost.'

dialogues.line: "Let's not overcomplicate this—Victor Vance was spotted sneaking out of the Study around 8:05 PM, and everyone heard Arthur shouting at 8:55. This is a panicked family job over the Will, plain and simple."

dialogues.target: Say to Thomas Graves (#3) [after Exhibit C]:
dialogues.line: "Careful chasing ghosts in a half-burned 2008 audit page. Someone cut the power at nine sharp and someone tampered with the wine—focus on who had the motive to stop the Will tonight!"

"Look, Clara Sterling, I don't care what a dusty 2008 ledger says—you were standing right beside Celeste Moreau in the Grand Hall when Arthur was shouting at 8:55! Tell everyone how you could possibly be in two places at once!"

characters.name: Clara Sterling
characters.special: YOU ARE THE KILLER! Win by avoiding indictment in the Final Verdict (frame Harriet Vance-Cole #8 or Victor Vance #5!). Your Shadow Team allies: Harriet Vance-Cole (#8), Lady Evelyn Vance (#1). During Blackouts, wake up to Intimidate 1 guest OR Plant a False Lead.
characters.persona: Composed, razor-sharp attorney retained since 2005. You drafted Arthur's New Will and serve as the room's anchor for facts and timelines.
characters.secret: In 2008, YOU were behind "2008 Offshore Escrow — Forged Beneficiary Deed" (signed "C.S."). Tonight: at 8:15 PM you rigged the Chronos Automaton (8:55 PM voice + 9:00 PM carafe smash); at 8:35 PM you blackmailed Harriet Vance-Cole (#8) to cut the generator at 9:00 PM; at 8:42 PM you handed Arthur a wax-sealed private digestif vial laced with concentrated Aconite (he died at 8:48 PM). You stood next to Celeste Moreau (#7) at 8:55 PM for an alibi, then slipped up at 9:01 PM by claiming you saw his chalk-pale lips (he was face-down!), smelled 'bitter-almond wine,' and lied about the 8:48 PM watch.
characters.clue: STRATEGY: Stay calm! Let the room suspect Victor Vance (#5) for drugging the wine and Harriet Vance-Cole (#8) for the blackout and Exhibit C. If pressed on Exhibit E, claim Arthur's watch broke earlier or someone forged "C.S." to frame you!
characters.detention: Searched from Clara Sterling's Effects: A folded dinner napkin smudged with faint fireplace soot and an unsigned note in Clara Sterling's handwriting: "Speak to Arthur privately before the 9:00 PM announcement—he cannot open that 2008 file tonight."

dialogues.line: "I was standing right beside Celeste Moreau in the Grand Hall at 8:55 PM when Arthur was shouting! With guests coming and going all evening, who had access to Arthur's Bordeaux decanter tonight? Someone clearly poisoned that wine before nine."
"I rolled Arthur over at 9:01 to check his pulse—pure reflex! Don't get distracted by a half-burned 2008 page; ask Harriet Vance-Cole why the lights conveniently died at nine!"
"Yes, I handed Arthur a wax-sealed private digestif vial at 8:42 PM—completely harmless! If his watch stopped at 8:48, he must have dropped it before arguing at 8:55. Don't fall for a frame-up!"

characters.name: Thomas Graves
characters.special: SPECIAL ABILITY (BLACKOUT PHASE): During each Blackout, if you are NOT Detained, the Host wakes you alone to secretly read ONE guest's Sealed Detention Card for 12 seconds!
characters.persona: Dignified, observant butler who notices everything and speaks quietly. You have served Ravenshollow Manor since 1999.
characters.secret: You skimmed small sums from the wine cellar budget for your sister's medical bills (making you nervous about wine questions), though you are innocent of murder. You also brought a miniature field chemistry kit in your bag, which you will use between Acts II and III to produce Exhibit F (testing the wine vs. Arthur's cuff).
characters.clue: At 8:40 PM you poured a piping-hot cup of chamomile tea in the Study—by 9:02 PM the untouched cup was barely lukewarm. You also saw Arthur's watch smashed at 8:48 PM.
characters.detention: Searched from Graves's Coat Pocket: Tonight's butler log: '8:40 PM — Poured hot cup of chamomile tea in Study. 9:02 PM — Cup untouched and barely lukewarm; watch crystal smashed at 8:48 PM.'

dialogues.line: "I did a headcount in the Grand Hall when the clock struck nine. You weren't there. Where exactly were you when the lights went out?"

"Wait a second—Exhibit D's Study re-inspection shows Arthur was slumped face-down at 9:01 PM, yet you claimed you saw his pale lips the instant the lights returned—and the puddle was odorless water, not wine!"

dialogues.target: Say to Victor Vance (#5) [after Exhibit F]:
dialogues.line: "My field test found chloral hydrate—sleeping powder—in the red wine decanter. Tell the truth right now, or you're getting my final vote!"

characters.name: Victor Vance
characters.persona: Charming, desperate nephew who owes $400,000 to dangerous creditors and desperately needed Arthur's inheritance.
characters.secret: RED HERRING! At 7:58 PM, you snuck into the Dining & Sideboard and put CHLORAL HYDRATE (non-lethal sleeping powder) into Arthur's 1998 Bordeaux wine decanter before a glass was carried up to his Study, then slipped into the Study around 8:05 PM to locate the New Will! You're terrified you killed him—until Exhibit F proves he never drank the wine!
characters.clue: Once Exhibit F drops in Act III, confess to the sleeping powder so the room stops wasting votes on you and hunts the real killer!
characters.detention: Searched from Victor Vance's Pocket: A folded white paper packet labeled 'Chloral Hydrate (Sleep Aid)' and a desperate note about stealing the unsigned New Will.

dialogues.line: "Keep your voice down! Yes, I stepped into the Study around 8:05 PM to talk to Arthur—he wasn't even there! Why is everyone blaming the wine?"
"Between us—did Lord Arthur drink any of that red wine tonight? Clara Sterling claimed it smelled of poison, and I'm worried..."

dialogues.target: Confess to Thomas Graves (#3) [after Exhibit F]:
dialogues.line: "Fine! I put sleeping powder—chloral hydrate—in the Bordeaux decanter in the Dining & Sideboard at 7:58 PM to steal the Will! NOT Aconite! And Exhibit F proves he NEVER DRANK THE WINE! I'm a thief, not a murderer!"

characters.name: Jasper Moore
characters.persona: Intense Chief Engineer who maintains the manor's backup generator and knows the Chronos Automaton inside and out.
characters.secret: You have been secretly selling Vance Precision clockwork blueprints to a rival tech CEO—you were in the basement hallway at 8:50 PM hiding a schematic tube!
characters.clue: You know the manor's backup generator breaker can only be cut manually from the basement Generator Room—the storm did NOT cause a clean 15-second blackout.
characters.detention: Searched from Jasper's Tool Roll: A rolled-up Vance Precision gear blueprint tucked inside a brass tube with a note: 'Wire $150k upon delivery.' (Corporate espionage, not murder!)

dialogues.line: "I built the backup power system in this manor, and I'm telling you right now: the storm did NOT cause a clean 15-second blackout. Someone manually pulled the main breaker in the basement Generator Room!"

dialogues.target: Say to Celeste Moreau (#7) [after Exhibit D]:
dialogues.line: "Look at Exhibit D—the Automaton's counterweight cam was shifted exactly two inches to strike the water carafe at 9:00 PM sharp. That takes deliberate calibration, not luck!"
"Think like an engineer: the 9:00 PM blackout and the 9:00 PM counterweight drop happened on the exact same chime. Whoever pulled that basement breaker was working for the real killer!"

characters.name: Celeste Moreau
characters.persona: Brilliant, fiercely proud master clockmaker and Arthur's former fiancée (he stole your escapement design 30 years ago). Invited to appraise the Chronos Automaton.
characters.secret: At 8:20 PM, you snuck upstairs to peek at the Automaton and saw a figure in a dark coat slip silently out of Arthur's Study carrying a small dark case.
characters.clue: You know the Chronos Automaton can be programmed to play a pre-recorded brass cylinder at 8:55 PM AND drop its 5-lb counterweight at 9:00 PM—proving Arthur could have died BEFORE 8:55!
characters.detention: Searched from Celeste's Handbag: A 30-year-old patent blueprint signed 'C. Moreau' ('He stole my life's work') PLUS a sketch showing the Automaton's timer gear can be set 60 minutes ahead.

dialogues.line: "Alright, I snuck up to the gallery at 8:20 PM for a glimpse of the Automaton—and right as I reached the top of the stairs, I saw a figure in a dark coat slip out of Arthur's Study carrying a small dark case!"

dialogues.target: Say to Lady Evelyn Vance (#1) [after Exhibit D]:
dialogues.line: "Mon Dieu—look at Exhibit D! The Chronos Automaton can play a pre-recorded brass cylinder at 8:55 PM AND drop its 5-pound counterweight at 9:00 PM! Arthur could have been dead BEFORE 8:55!"

"The Automaton's counterweight was shifted two inches to smash that carafe at 9:00 PM—the exact second the lights went out while you were missing from the Grand Hall. Don't tell me that's a coincidence!"

characters.name: Harriet Vance-Cole
characters.special: YOU ARE ON THE SHADOW TEAM! You are allied with Clara Sterling (#2) and win ONLY if the Killer escapes indictment in the Final Verdict. Fellow accomplice: Lady Evelyn Vance (#1). Wake up with the Shadow Team during Blackout Phases.
characters.persona: Sharp-eyed retired magistrate estranged from Arthur because you suspected he covered up something rotten back in 2008.
characters.secret: Clara Sterling (#2) caught your private scandal and blackmailed you into cutting the basement generator breaker for 15 seconds at 9:00 PM sharp! You didn't know Clara Sterling was going to murder Arthur, but if Clara Sterling goes down, you go to prison as an accessory. Worse, your initials (H.V.) appear on the burned Exhibit C audit log from 2008—even though you had no access in 2008!
characters.clue: STRATEGY: Deflect suspicion onto Victor Vance (#5) and defend Clara Sterling's (#2) 8:55 PM Grand Hall alibi!
characters.detention: Searched from Harriet Vance-Cole's Belongings: Heavy rubber-insulated electrical gloves (smelling of ozone from the generator breaker) and an unsigned blackmail note: '9:00 PM sharp. Fifteen seconds of dark, or your secret goes to the police.'

dialogues.line: "I wasn't in the Grand Hall at nine because I heard a shutter banging near the basement stairs. Stop pointing fingers at me when everyone knows Victor Vance was desperate to stop that Will tonight!"

dialogues.target: Say to Chef Henri Laurent (#9) [after Exhibit C]:
dialogues.line: "Look at Exhibit C—2008! Yes, 'H.V.' was flagged on that burned page, but I had NO access to Archive Box #4 in 2008 and nothing to do with '2008 Offshore Escrow — Forged Beneficiary Deed'! You're barking up the wrong tree!"
"I didn't touch any poison and I didn't rig that Automaton! Look at who stood to gain from the unsigned Will—and remember Clara Sterling was in the Grand Hall at 8:55!"

characters.name: Chef Henri Laurent
characters.persona: Dramatic, fiercely proud head chef—offended anyone would suggest Arthur was poisoned by your food or wine!
characters.secret: At 7:58 PM in the Dining & Sideboard, you saw someone hovering nervously over the opened 1998 Bordeaux decanter with a tiny white paper packet.
characters.clue: 1) At 8:40 PM a piping-hot cup of chamomile tea was poured in the Study—by 9:02 PM the untouched cup was barely lukewarm. 2) At 8:42 PM, YOU PERSONALLY SAW Clara Sterling (#2) hand Arthur a wax-sealed private digestif vial in the Grand Hall right before Arthur locked himself in the Study!
characters.detention: Searched from Chef Henri Laurent's Pocket: Tonight's handwritten note: '8:40 PM — Hot cup of chamomile tea poured in Study. 8:42 PM — Watched Clara Sterling (#2) hand Arthur a wax-sealed private digestif vial in the Grand Hall. 9:02 PM — Tea untouched & barely lukewarm; watch smashed at 8:48 PM.'

dialogues.line: "Did you see anyone near Lord Arthur's Study around 8:20 PM? Something about this 9:00 PM timeline doesn't add up—his watch smashed at 8:48!"
"The wine glass on Arthur's desk was completely full. What troubles me is the single cup of hot chamomile tea poured at 8:40 PM—by 9:02 PM, it was untouched and barely lukewarm!"
"Think back! At 8:42 PM in the Grand Hall, I personally watched Clara Sterling (#2) hand Arthur a wax-sealed private digestif vial—and Arthur carried it straight up to his locked Study!"

characters.name: Margot Bell
characters.persona: Sharp Boston Chronicle reporter who secretly crashed the gala posing as a guest's plus-one to investigate Arthur's 2008 cover-up.
characters.secret: You paid your way onto the guest list under a fake name to hunt for Archive Box #4 in the manor library.
characters.clue: You carry a 2008 newspaper clipping confirming Archive Box #4 implicates someone who held an active 2008 role in Exhibit E—NOT someone who had no 2008 access!
characters.detention: Searched from Margot's Bag: A Boston Chronicle press pass and a 2008 clipping noting the Archive Box #4 cover-up was buried by Arthur Vance in November 2008.

dialogues.line: "Forgive my curiosity, but I heard Arthur's New Will creates a transparency foundation. Does it unseal Archive Box #4 from November 2008?"

dialogues.target: Say to Harriet Vance-Cole (#8) [after Exhibit C]:
dialogues.line: "Interesting—I happen to carry a 2008 Boston Chronicle clipping about Archive Box #4. It implicates someone professionally active in 2008. Where were you working in 2008?"

dialogues.target: Say to Clara Sterling (#2) [after Exhibit E]:
dialogues.line: "I'm actually an investigative reporter with the Boston Chronicle. My 2008 clipping matches Exhibit E—check who was actually in that 2008 role and cross off everyone who wasn't!"

characters.name: Sebastian Cole
characters.persona: Suave antique appraiser with a suspicious habit of disappearing into side rooms.
characters.secret: Drowning in auction debt, you snuck into the upstairs gallery at 8:45 PM to swap a priceless Fabergé clock with a replica! You're an art thief, NOT a killer.
characters.clue: At 8:48 PM, while hiding behind a curtain in the upstairs gallery, you heard a heavy muffled THUMP inside Arthur's locked Study—followed by dead silence!
characters.detention: Searched from Sebastian's Coat: A counterfeit brass Fabergé clock wrapped in velvet and a pawnshop receipt. (Art thief, NOT a murderer!)

dialogues.line: "Don't let anyone tell you Arthur was alive and well at 8:50. I was... admiring the upstairs gallery around 8:48 PM, and I distinctly heard a heavy, muffled THUMP inside his locked Study—followed by dead silence."

dialogues.target: Say to Celeste Moreau (#7) [after Exhibit D]:
dialogues.line: "You know clockwork better than anyone here—could the Automaton play a voice at 8:55 and drop a counterweight at 9:00? Because whatever thumped at 8:48 PM sounded like a man hitting the floor!"
"Fine, I had no business lingering in the upstairs gallery at 8:48 PM—I was eyeing a Fabergé clock, alright? Arrest me for bad taste, not murder! But I swear Arthur collapsed at 8:48 PM!"

characters.name: Lydia Vance
characters.persona: Icy, ambitious, and furious with Victor (#5) for gambling away your savings.
characters.secret: At 8:35 PM near the basement stairs, you overheard two people whispering furiously: 'Fifteen seconds of dark at nine sharp, or your secret goes to the police!'
characters.clue: You know for a fact that the 9:00 PM blackout was a deliberate blackmail job—NOT a storm surge!
characters.detention: Searched from Lydia's Purse: Signed divorce papers naming Victor's $400k debt, plus a cocktail napkin note: '8:35 PM basement stairs — overheard: 15 seconds of dark at 9 sharp or secret goes to police.'

dialogues.line: "Look me in the eye. If you did something desperate with that wine tonight because of money, I am not going down with you."

"Funny thing—at 8:35 PM near the basement stairs, I overheard two people whispering furiously: 'Fifteen seconds of dark at nine sharp, or your secret goes to the police!' Care to tell me who was blackmailing you?"
"Stop blaming the storm for the 9:00 PM blackout! I overheard the blackmail threat on the basement stairs at 8:35 PM—whoever cut the lights was forced into it by the real killer!"

characters.name: Father Silas Ward
characters.persona: Gentle, solemn parish priest who has been Arthur Vance's spiritual confessor for twenty years.
characters.secret: Last Tuesday, Arthur confessed he had spent eighteen years 'shielding a guilty soul from a 2008 sin.' Bound by the Seal of Confession, you speak in pointed truths.
characters.clue: You know Arthur's New Will was his final act of penance to expose the true culprit from 2008.
characters.detention: Searched from Father Silas's Breviary: A Nov 14 bookmark in Arthur's hand: 'Father, pray for me. On the 19th I am ending eighteen years of silence about Archive Box #4.'

dialogues.line: "I have been Arthur's confessor for twenty years. Last Tuesday he came to me burdened by eighteen years of shielding a guilty soul from a 2008 sin he could no longer keep buried."

dialogues.target: Say to Thomas Graves (#3) [after Exhibit C]:
dialogues.line: "I am bound by the Seal of Confession, so listen carefully: Arthur's New Will was his final act of penance to unseal Archive Box #4. The guilty soul feared the truth of 2008 far more than losing an inheritance."

dialogues.target: Say to Victor Vance (#5) [after Exhibit E]:
dialogues.line: "Look past the noise of the 9:00 PM blackout and read Exhibit E with clear eyes. The person who truly belonged to that 2008 sin is the one who silenced Arthur before he could sign."

characters.name: Damien Cross
characters.persona: Tough, cynical head of security who knows every corridor, lock, and blind spot in Ravenshollow Manor.
characters.secret: You were paid years ago to bury corporate PR headaches for Arthur—and you're terrified of federal subpoenas.
characters.clue: You inspected the Study door at 9:01 PM and confirmed the steel deadbolt was genuinely thrown from the inside—meaning the poison entered the room WITH Arthur at 8:45 PM.
characters.detention: Searched from Damien's Jacket: A security log confirming the Study deadbolt was bolted from inside, plus an old NDA from Vance Precision.

dialogues.line: "As head of security, I inspected the Study door at 9:01 PM myself—the steel deadbolt was genuinely thrown from the inside. Nobody walked in or out after Arthur locked it at 8:45 PM."

dialogues.target: Say to Celeste Moreau (#7) [after Exhibit D]:
dialogues.line: "Think tactically: if the Study deadbolt was locked from inside at 8:45, the ONLY way to stage an 8:55 shout and a 9:00 crash was a rigged mechanical timer inside the room!"

dialogues.target: Say to Chef Henri Laurent (#9) [after Exhibit F]:
dialogues.line: "Locked door from the inside means the Aconite walked into the Study WITH Arthur at 8:45 PM. Whoever handed him something at 8:42 PM in the Grand Hall is our killer!"

characters.name: Vivienne Sterling
characters.persona: Meticulous, ambitious junior attorney who personally typed up Arthur's New Will this afternoon.
characters.secret: You secretly copied the corporate restructuring pages onto a thumb drive to shop to a rival firm—shady ambition, NOT murder.
characters.clue: At 4:00 PM today in the library, you caught someone alone reading Page 14 (the 2008 Archive Box #4 clause) of the New Will—they went pale as a ghost!
characters.detention: Searched from Vivienne's Portfolio: A 4:00 PM legal sticky note: 'Caught a guest reading Page 14 (2008 Archive Box #4 clause) of the New Will in the library. They looked terrified.'

dialogues.line: "I probably should have mentioned this sooner—at 4:00 PM today in the Library, I caught a guest alone reading Page 14 (the 2008 Archive Box #4 clause) of the New Will, and they went pale as a ghost!"

dialogues.target: Say to Thomas Graves (#3) [after Exhibit C]:
dialogues.line: "I typed up the New Will myself this afternoon. Arthur added the Archive Box #4 release clause at the very last minute—whoever read Page 14 at 4:00 PM realized they had until 9:00 PM to stop him!"

dialogues.target: Say to Victor Vance (#5) [after Exhibit E]:
dialogues.line: "You didn't even know about Page 14's 2008 clause, did you? You only cared about the inheritance. Look at Exhibit E—the real killer was terrified of Archive Box #4!"

characters.name: Nadia Vance
characters.persona: Brilliant pharmacology student whose medical school tuition is funded by the Vance family trust.
characters.secret: You borrowed rare botanical specimens from the university conservatory for an unauthorized thesis experiment—academic misconduct, NOT murder.
characters.clue: As a pharmacology student, you know concentrated Aconite is completely odorless and fatal within 2–3 minutes—totally different from bitter-almond cyanide!
characters.detention: Searched from Nadia's Clutch: Lab notes comparing Chloral Hydrate (non-lethal sedative) vs. Aconite (odorless, fatal in 2–3 minutes).

dialogues.line: "As a pharmacology student, something bothers me: cyanide has a strong bitter-almond odor, whereas concentrated Aconite is completely odorless and stops the heart in two to three minutes!"

"Look at Exhibit D's Study re-inspection—the puddle on the floor was clear, odorless water, and the wine glass wasn't even touched. Whoever claimed to smell 'bitter almonds from the wine' was steering us away from an odorless poison!"

dialogues.target: Say to Clara Sterling (#2) [after Exhibit F]:
dialogues.line: "Exhibit F confirms my hunch! Chloral Hydrate in the wine is just a non-lethal sedative, while concentrated Aconite on Arthur's lips kills in 2–3 minutes—matching an 8:45 PM dose and an 8:48 PM collapse!"

characters.name: Capt. Roderick Hale
characters.persona: Booming, weathered retired naval navigator stranded at the manor by the washed-out bridge.
characters.secret: You're obsessed with precision timekeeping—at 8:55 PM you checked your U.S. Naval Observatory chronometer against the manor's Grand Clock (dead-on to the second).
characters.clue: Yesterday afternoon at the pier, you synced your naval chronometer with Arthur's pocket watch! Arthur's watch did NOT run 12 minutes slow—whoever claimed that in Act I was LYING!
characters.detention: Searched from Capt. Hale's Pea Coat: A brass U.S. Naval Observatory chronometer and harbor log: '14:00 — Synchronized with Arthur Vance. His gold pocket watch is accurate to ±0.1 sec.'

dialogues.line: "Hold everything! Someone just claimed Arthur's pocket watch ran twelve minutes slow? Hogwash! I synced my U.S. Naval Observatory chronometer with Arthur's watch at the pier yesterday—dead-on to the second!"

dialogues.target: Say to Celeste Moreau (#7) [after Exhibit D]:
dialogues.line: "If Arthur's watch never lost a second and smashed at 8:48 PM, then whoever we heard yelling at 8:55 PM wasn't Arthur—unless ghosts can shout through oak doors, it had to be that brass cylinder!"

dialogues.target: Say to Clara Sterling (#2) [after Exhibit E]:
dialogues.line: "Arthur's Horologist Journal in Exhibit E backs me up 100%! His watch stopped at 8:48 PM—which means whoever snapped that watch lid shut and called it 'twelve minutes slow' lied to this entire room!"

characters.name: Alistair Finch
characters.persona: Theatrical, scatterbrained ghostwriter living at the manor for two months to write Arthur's tell-all memoirs.
characters.secret: Arthur fired you yesterday for peeking at his sealed Archive Box #4 (making you look bitter!), though you are innocent of murder.
characters.clue: Two days ago, you helped Arthur record Chapter 12 of his memoirs onto a blank brass cylinder—word-for-word: 'You've gone too far! I'm calling the police as soon as the lines are back!'
characters.detention: Searched from Alistair's Notebook: Nov 17 shorthand notes: 'Recorded Arthur's Ch. 12 quote onto brass cylinder (You've gone too far! I'm calling the police!). Subject: 2008 Archive Box #4 cover-up.'

dialogues.line: "Don't you find it extraordinary? The exact words we heard Arthur shouting at 8:55 PM—'You've gone too far! I'm calling the police as soon as the lines are back!'—are word-for-word from Chapter 12 of the memoir he dictated to me two days ago!"

dialogues.target: Say to Celeste Moreau (#7) [after Exhibit D]:
dialogues.line: "I personally helped Arthur record Chapter 12 onto a blank brass cylinder two days ago and watched him set it beside the Automaton! If that cylinder is inside Exhibit D, someone swapped it to fake his voice!"

dialogues.target: Say to Celeste Moreau (#7) [after Exhibit E]:
dialogues.line: "Arthur fired me yesterday just for peeking at his sealed Archive Box #4! Chapter 12 of his memoir was all about that 2008 cover-up—and Exhibit E finally names the culprit he was protecting!"

exhibits.title: Exhibit A — Study Crime Scene Sketch (9:02 PM)
exhibits.html:
• Door & Window: Heavy oak double-door bolted from the inside; cliff window latched inside.
  • The Body: Lord Arthur Vance slumped across his desk blotter. First reached and rolled over by Clara Sterling (#2) at 9:01 PM.
  • Initial Statement (9:01 PM): As guests rushed in, Clara Sterling (#2) loudly claimed to see Arthur's "chalk-pale lips" and smell "bitter almonds from the spilled wine."
  • On the Desk: Unsigned New Will; a crystal wine glass; a single poured porcelain cup of chamomile tea (barely lukewarm by 9:02 PM); a broken pocket watch.
  • On the Floor: Shattered glass beside a heavy 5-lb brass counterweight in a pool of spilled liquid.

exhibits.title: Exhibit B — Arthur's Shattered Pocket Watch
exhibits.html:
• Make: Custom Vance Precision Gold Chronometer ("A.V. — Time Never Lies").
  • Condition: Crystal cracked; internal gears jammed from hitting the desk corner.
  • Frozen Time: 8:48 PM (12 minutes before the 9:00 PM blackout).
  • Witness Note: Clara Sterling (#2) snapped the gold lid shut at 9:01 PM, claiming Arthur's watch "always ran twelve minutes slow."

exhibits.title: Exhibit C — Charred Audit Log ('C.S.' / 'H.V.')
exhibits.html:
VANCE PRECISION INSTRUMENTS — CONFIDENTIAL AUDIT
ARCHIVE BOX #4 (SLATED FOR RELEASE WITH NEW WILL)
-------------------------------------------------
SUBJECT:   2008 Offshore Escrow — Forged Beneficiary Deed
FINDING:   Trust signature forged to liquidate a partner's estate in Nov 2008
FLAGGED INITIALS: "C.S." / "H.V." [ROLES & DATES BURNED]
NOTE:      One party falsified the 2008 record; the other had
           no 2008 access to Archive Box #4.
STATUS:    Suppressed by A. Vance (2008). Full disclosure
           ordered upon execution of New Will.

exhibits.title: Exhibit D — Chronos Automaton, Wax Cylinder & Study Re-Inspection
exhibits.html:
• Phonograph Drum: Plays a removable brass wax cylinder at a scheduled minute. Currently set to 8:55 PM.
  • Release Cam: Drops a 5-lb brass counterweight at 9:00 PM (shifted 2 inches to strike the water carafe).
  • Cylinder Label: Reads "9:00 PM Gala Greeting" — hastily glued over a scratched-out title: "Memoir Draft — Confrontation."
  • Study Re-Inspection (Clear Light): The crystal wine glass on the desk is completely full & untouched; the shattered glass on the floor is a water carafe in clear, odorless liquid (zero wine, zero bitter-almond scent). Desk-blotter impressions confirm Arthur collapsed face-down, facing away from the door until Clara Sterling (#2) rolled him over.

exhibits.title: Exhibit E — 2008 Dossier Ledger & Horologist Journal
exhibits.html:
• Selected 2008 Archive Records:
    • Lady Evelyn Vance (#1): Director of Vance Charity Gala Fund (2006–2008)
    • Clara Sterling (#2): Lead Trust Counsel, Vance Legal Holdings (2005–present)
    • Thomas Graves (#3): Estate Steward & Keyholder, Ravenshollow (1999–present)
    • Victor Vance (#5): Junior Commodities Broker, Vance Capital (2007–2008)
    • Celeste Moreau (#7): Master Appraiser, Geneva Horology Guild (2008)
    • Harriet Vance-Cole (#8): No access to Archive Box #4 in 2008 (outside the 2008 incident window).
  • Arthur's Horologist Journal (Nov 15): "A clockmaker whose own pocket watch loses a single second is a fraud. My gold chronometer is calibrated daily to the U.S. Naval Observatory signal. It has not drifted by half a second in eleven years."

exhibits.title: Exhibit F — Field Toxicology Report
exhibits.html:
• Red Wine (Dining Sideboard Decanter & Untouched Study Glass): Positive for Chloral Hydrate (non-lethal sleeping sedative). Arthur never drank it.
  • Residue on Arthur's Lips & Cuff: Positive for Concentrated Aconite (fast-acting, completely odorless cardiac poison; fatal in 2–3 minutes) — matching trace contact from a wax-sealed private digestif vial.
  • Floor Puddle: Plain spring water. Zero wine, zero bitter-almond odor.

exhibits.title: False Lead #1 — Crumpled Generator Note (Blackout Action)
exhibits.html:
Found crumpled on the basement stairs immediately after the blackout:

"9:00 PM sharp. Pull the main breaker. Don't let anyone see you. — V.V."

exhibits.title: False Lead #2 — Anonymous Library Rumor (Blackout Action)
exhibits.html:
Slipped under the Library door during the blackout:

"Check the Dining & Sideboard! Someone wiped down the Bordeaux decanter left on the sideboard with an almond-scented handkerchief right before 9:00 PM."

prologue.label: PROLOGUE — 9:00 PM
prologue.sub: Read aloud (or click Read Aloud) to set the scene at Ravenshollow Manor.
prologue.html:
Welcome to Ravenshollow Manor. Outside, a violent November nor'easter has washed out the wooden bridge to the mainland, and the telephone lines are dead. You are guests of billionaire clockmaker Lord Arthur Vance (72).

At 8:45 PM, Arthur retired alone to his second-floor Study to fetch his New Will, bolting the heavy oak door from the inside. At 8:55 PM, guests in the Grand Hall heard Arthur shouting from upstairs: "You've gone too far! I'm calling the police as soon as the lines are back!"

At 9:00 PM sharp, as the Grand Astronomical Clock struck nine, the backup generator died—plunging the manor into darkness for 15 seconds. A sharp crack and heavy thud echoed from the Study. When the lights returned at 9:01 PM, you broke down the bolted door—and found Arthur Vance dead at his desk.

act1.label: ACT I — THE LOCKED STUDY (7 MIN)
act1.sub: Read Public Opener, unlock Exhibits A & B, mingle (7m), then Vote (3m) & Blackout (1m).
act1.html:
Chef Henri Laurent (#9)
"Nobody touch a thing! The oak door was bolted from the inside, and the window drops eighty feet to the rocks. How on earth could someone kill him in a locked room?"
Celeste Moreau (#7)
"He was shouting at someone at 8:55! We all heard him! Then at 9:00 the lights went out and—my God, was that a gunshot?"
Clara Sterling (#2)
"There is no bullet wound. It was poison! The moment the lights came back on at 9:01, I saw Arthur's chalk-pale lips and smelled that unmistakable bitter-almond scent from the spilled wine. He died right around nine."
Chef Henri Laurent (#9)
"Begging your pardon, but when I stepped beside the desk, I noticed Lord Arthur's pocket watch had smashed on the corner—its hands were stopped at 8:48."
Clara Sterling (#2)
"Ah, yes, I closed the lid so it wouldn't upset everyone. Arthur's watch always ran twelve minutes slow—he told me so himself just yesterday."
Thomas Graves (#3)
"Slow or not, the New Will is still on his desk—unsigned. Whoever wanted Arthur dead before 9:00 PM is standing in this room."

blackout1.sub: 100% Spoiler-Free Automated Blackout — everyone closes their eyes!
blackout1.html: Click Start Auto-Blackout below (or in the top bar). The app will narrate the entire Blackout phase aloud—waking the Shadow Team to make a silent tap, then waking the Inspector to privately inspect 1 Detention Card—so nobody has to sit out as a human host!

act2.label: ACT II — SHADOWS IN THE CLOCKWORK (6 MIN)
act2.sub: Read Public Opener, unlock Exhibits C & D, mingle (6m), then Vote (3m) & Blackout (1m).
act2.html:
Thomas Graves (#3)
"While the upstairs gallery was cleared, we inspected the Study fireplace and the Chronos Automaton. We have two new exhibits—a half-burned 2008 audit log flagging the initials 'C.S.' and 'H.V.', and a scratched brass wax cylinder inside the Automaton."
Celeste Moreau (#7)
"Wait—a scratched cylinder? Arthur built the Chronos Automaton to play a recorded greeting at 9:00 PM. You can also program its brass counterweight to drop on the hour. If someone swapped the cylinder..."
Harriet Vance-Cole (#8)
"Don't look at me just because 'H.V.' is on that burned page! Half the people in this house had a reason to hate Arthur. And if you're wondering why the lights went out at nine, the storm probably surged the old breaker!"
Victor Vance (#5)
"Oh, spare us! And what about the wine? Clara Sterling said it smelled of poison—who poured Arthur's glass?!"
Chef Henri Laurent (#9)
"Actually... look at our Study re-inspection on Exhibit D. In clear light, the wine glass on the desk is completely full and untouched—it was the water carafe that shattered in odorless water, and Arthur was slumped face-down!"

act3.label: ACT III — THE LAST CHIME (7 MIN)
act3.sub: Read Public Opener, unlock Exhibits E & F, mingle (7m), then Final Verdict (3m) & Reveal!
act3.html:
Thomas Graves (#3)
"Enough games. We unlocked Arthur's private Horologist Journal and the 2008 Archive Ledger—and tested the residue in the Study with a field chemistry kit."
Chef Henri Laurent (#9)
"Look closely at Exhibit E and Exhibit F before you cast your final vote. The single cup of chamomile tea poured at 8:40 PM was untouched and barely lukewarm by 9:02 PM—and Arthur never touched his wine."
Clara Sterling (#2)
"Careful, everyone—wild theories will only let the real killer slip away. Look at who had the motive to steal the Will, who rigged the power, and who wasn't in the Grand Hall at nine. Let's settle this."

revealHtml:
The Truth Behind the Last Chime (RV-1860)

The Killer: Clara Sterling (#2)
The Accomplices (Shadow Team): Harriet Vance-Cole (#8), Lady Evelyn Vance (#1)
The Inspector: Thomas Graves (#3)

Arthur Vance did not die at 9:00 PM. He died at 8:48 PM—alone behind a bolted door—from concentrated Aconite hidden in the wax-sealed private digestif vial handed to him by Clara Sterling (#2) at 8:42 PM.

Victor Vance (#5) spiked the red wine with harmless sleeping powder, which Arthur never touched. The 8:55 PM argument was a pre-recorded brass wax cylinder played by the Chronos Automaton, and the 9:00 PM crash was the counterweight smashing the water carafe while blackmailed accomplice Harriet Vance-Cole (#8) cut the generator breaker for 15 seconds.

The 4-Pillar Proof: (1) Arthur's pocket watch froze at 8:48 PM and his Horologist Journal proves it never lost a second; (2) The wine was untouched and Arthur died of odorless Aconite from the wax-sealed private digestif vial; (3) Clara Sterling slipped up in Act I by claiming to see Arthur's pale lips (Arthur was face-down!) and smell bitter almonds from spilled wine (it was odorless water!); (4) Exhibit C flagged both "C.S." and "H.V.", but Exhibit E clears Harriet Vance-Cole (no 2008 access) and ties Clara Sterling directly to 2008 Offshore Escrow — Forged Beneficiary Deed (Lead Trust Counsel, Vance Legal Holdings (2005–present))!
